A1.justification: Both PDFs describe BioAgent Bench. All 18 pages in each version, including figures, tables and Appendices A.1–A.8, support comparison. Sections and tables can be matched despite reorganization.

before.justification: v3 reports original model and harness evaluations, planning scores, repeated-trial stability measurements and perturbation outcomes.

after.justification: v4 retains original completion results, planning analysis, stability measurements and perturbation experiments in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The evaluation harness, artifact-based workflow, GPT-5.1 grader and grading rules retain the same procedures. Appendix prompt edits correct grammar without changing their substantive instructions.

E1.justification: The same ten bioinformatics tasks, underlying datasets and corruption, decoy and prompt-bloat scenarios are retained. The GIAB stability entries added to the merged table are NA, not an additional evaluation.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains unchanged in the completion, planning and harness comparisons. Figure 2 relabels GPT-5.1 as GPT-5.1-Codex-Max, consistent with the existing 81.67% appendix entry; this does not introduce a new comparator.

E3.justification: Most settings remain unchanged, including resource limits, harnesses, grading and metric calculations. However, v4 Table 2 describes stability in intermediate outputs, whereas both versions' main text describes final results and Appendix A.6 retains the same result columns. The PDFs do not resolve whether this is a caption error or a revised evaluation target.

E4.justification: The planning analysis, repeated-trial stability analysis, three perturbation tests and associated failure cases are retained. Appendix A.7 contains the same four-log Salmon configuration case study. Combining the robustness tables adds no new analysis.

E5.justification: v4 explicitly identifies the main completion results as single-run and explains that GIAB was run only once. Its merged Table 2 removes per-task trial counts: v3 explicitly reports three cystic-fibrosis trials, while v4 gives a general four-trial caption. This changes reporting without establishing additional runs. No confidence intervals or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: Figure 2 changes GLM-4.7's comparative-genomics, deseq and giab scores from 75/75/0 to 50/100/75, raising its displayed average from 75.0% to 82.5% and changing its ranking. The unchanged appendix already reports 75.0% for OpenCode and 82.5% for Codex CLI, so this is not an established same-setting gain. The results prose also changes error-loop attribution from closed-source to open-weight models.

T1.justification: Neither version introduces theoretical propositions or proofs. v4 omits the displayed standard Jaccard formula while retaining the metric; this removes an explanation rather than revising mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The benchmark, model comparison and evaluation-suite contributions remain the same. High completion with minimal scaffolding, weaker open-weight performance, unreliable step-level behavior and the motivation for private local agents are retained claims. v4 emphasizes these points differently without materially changing their scope.

C2.justification: v4 adds an explicit rationale that relaxing resource constraints would limit evaluation breadth and depth, and explains GIAB's missing stability measurements through resource requirements. Its planning discussion states the domain-knowledge versus agentic-capability inference more definitively. The substantive grading, realism and robustness limitations otherwise remain.

D1.justification: Figure 3 newly explains that GPT-5.1 was excluded from planning comparisons because it graded the plans; it was already absent in v3. Conversely, v4 omits v3's explicit GPT-5.2/Codex CLI attribution in the perturbation section. Appendix implementation details and the two repository destinations remain equivalent.

R1.justification: v4 adds SWE-Bench Pro (Deng et al., 2025) and a short discussion of HeurekaBench/sc-HeurekaBench (Panigrahi et al., 2026). The broader positioning is retained. Other reference changes largely update bibliographic information for existing works.

P1.justification: The abstract and substantial portions of the introduction, definitions, setup, results and discussion are rewritten. Related Work moves from Section 2 to Section 9, perturbation analysis becomes a standalone section, and new paragraph headings reorganize the narrative. Terminology and publication headers are also standardized.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is substantially redesigned and simplified. Figures 2–3 change visual encodings, labels and legends, including replacing heatmap task names with icons. Table 1 adds icons and explicit Yes/No labels. The separate stability and perturbation tables become one full-width table with revised columns and caption.

improvement.justification: v4 improves internal consistency by aligning Figure 2's GLM-4.7 average with the already reported appendix result and correcting model labels and failure attribution. Reorganized exposition clarifies the retained work. These gains are limited by the merged robustness table's loss of the cystic-fibrosis trial-count exception and its intermediate-versus-final-output ambiguity; the revision provides no substantial new empirical validation.
